data.description:
## Context / Problem
rebar mints only Ed25519 op-certs (all 3,883 live SIGNATURE events on this tracker), and story 8f1d's contract phase already refuses the legacy HMAC-SHA256 scheme for both op-cert kinds, yet the HMAC module, its key custody (`REBAR_SIGNING_KEY`, `<tracker>/.signing-key`), and a verify path with no producer remain. The operator ruled on 2026-09-06 to retire it entirely, having confirmed that the store keeps parsing (the reducer never imports the module; 688 tickets' folded snapshots carry HMAC entries, 1,124 on closed or deleted tickets and 1 on an open ticket) and that the worst case is one re-review of an already-not-certified attestation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No HMAC signing, key custody, or verification code remains, `rebar init` no longer mints a key file, and a non-envelope SIGNATURE record verifies `unsigned` with a reason naming the retired scheme on the CLI, MCP, and plan-review status surfaces. Checked by the retirement story's greps and its new test module.
- [ ] Historical stores are unaffected: a folded snapshot carrying an HMAC attestation still reduces, renders, and passes store validation. Checked by the fixture test built from a live snapshot shape.
- [ ] ADRs 0044 and 0049 carry the amendment, the env-var registry has no `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY` row, and the release notes state the break and migration. Checked by the docs assertions in the story.

## Child decomposition
- Retirement story: delivers all three criteria (one change; no dependency forces a split).
data.title: Retire the legacy HMAC-SHA256 signing scheme
